summary: The article describes how community theaters in the region are nurturing local talent through workshops and training programs launched in fall 2023. Programs cover acting, playwriting, backstage crafts, music and dance integration, youth theater, and an original-play festival. Participants and leaders say these programs build skills, teamwork, identity, and community belonging, keeping community theater a living tradition.
one_line: Regional community theaters launched fall 2023 workshops, youth programs, and a playwrights festival to train local talent and strengthen cultural identity.
key_facts: Grandview Community Playhouse began an extensive training program for all age groups on October 1, 2023, led by director Mark Thomson.
The Grandview program offers weekly acting workshops, month-long intensives for beginners and seasoned performers, and playwriting seminars led by award-winning playwright Lisa Gomez.
Riverside Cultural Center started a backstage workshop series on September 15, 2023, covering set design and construction, lighting, and sound engineering.
Omar Jenkins took the Riverside backstage workshop and ended up helping design the set for the latest production.
Larkspur Theatre Company started a collaborative training program on November 2, 2023, with Elmwood Dance Studio and the Harmony School of Music.
Larkspur artistic director Anne-Marie D'Souza says blending acting with music and dance brings 'an entirely different dimension to a performance.'
Maplewood Community Theater started its Youth Theater Initiative on September 20, 2023, with after-school acting classes, summer camps, and a junior production company.
Kevin O'Neil, a 12-year-old participant in the Maplewood youth program, says participants help build sets, choose costumes, and make storytelling decisions.
Oak Grove Arts Collective launched 'The New Voices Playwrights Festival' on December 1, 2023, giving chosen original plays a fully-supported production.
Emma Yu, a finalist in the festival, said seeing her play performed 'validated my voice as an artist in the community.'
Local actress Emily Stanton first stepped onto the stage at age eight and described theater as a second home.
Local historian Michael Johnson calls the workshops an investment in 'the cultural lifeblood of our town.'
